provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The external validity of the findings is unclear because biodiversity surveys are not randomly assigned to locations and species; the evaluator notes this as an unavoidable drawback of survey-based studies, though they judge the authors' discussion adequate.
issues.quote: this paper faces the unavoidable drawback that the external validity of its findings is unclear, because surveys are not randomly assigned to locations and species

issues.text: The environmental regulation (Clean Air Act) section is the least robust part of the paper, with the evaluator identifying it as the main area needing improvement.
issues.quote: The main area of focus of these comments relates to the section on environmental regulation, which I think is the least robust section of the paper.

issues.text: GDP is likely non-stationary while the biodiversity outcomes may be stationary, so using GDP to explain them may introduce substantial noise into the specification; state-level GDP trends are also heterogeneous, and year fixed effects only partly address this.
issues.quote: if the biodiversity outcome variables are stationary, then using a non-stationary variable (GDP) to explain these outcome variables may introduce a lot of noise into the specification

issues.text: The paper gives limited guidance on the economic magnitude of the estimated effects, making it hard for readers to judge how large the impacts are and their real-world relevance.
issues.quote: some further discussion could help guide the reader to understand how large these estimated impacts are and improve the real-world applicability of the paper

issues.text: The Clean Air Act analysis does not justify the choice of a count of NA designations rather than a binary indicator of any designation.
issues.quote: why use the count of NA designations rather than a binary variable to indicate any positive number of NA designations?

issues.text: The choice of an IV strategy for the Clean Air Act analysis is not justified; a difference-in-differences design around the 2005 PM2.5 NAAQS could be feasible and is not considered or tested as a robustness check.
issues.quote: Also, why use an IV strategy rather than an alternative approach such as difference-in-differences?

issues.text: The causal interpretation of the Clean Air Act estimates needs more discussion, in particular whether attainment affects biodiversity only through its effect on GDP (the exclusion restriction).
issues.quote: how confident can we be that attainment only affects biodiversity through its effect on GDP?

issues.text: The equation for the Section 5.1 empirical specification is not written out explicitly and readers must refer back to an earlier section, which hampers clarity and comparison with prior Clean Air Act literature.
issues.quote: It may be helpful to readers to see the equation for section 5.1 written out explicitly, rather than referring the reader to the previous section

issues.text: The heterogeneity analysis done for the GDP-biodiversity relationship is not extended to the regulation-biodiversity association, which could reveal which taxa are protected by regulation and how regulation effects vary across the biodiversity distribution.
issues.quote: it would be interesting to explore the heterogeneity in the pollution regulation-biodiversity association

issues.text: The abstract does not mention the heterogeneous findings (greater vulnerability of non-bird and especially mammal species, and of locations with already low biodiversity), which the evaluator considers a key novel contribution.
issues.quote: I would suggest mentioning them in the abstract.
